DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

NhdSlopeClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 flowline slope. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 31 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 23 of these curves carried forward unchanged from version 8. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

annotations.methodContext: Collect one D-frame net sample (500 micrometer mesh) one meter downstream of each of the 11 transects at the assigned left, center or right station, and composite them. A laboratory identifies a fixed count subsample. The value is the number of mayfly, stonefly and caddisfly taxa.
